title: Logistics Specialist (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
4.     MOS 0441, Logistics Specialist (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. The Logistics Specialist oversees the preparation of
supplies and equipment for embarkation and performs various force deployment
planning and execution (FDP&E) functions that support the movement of
personnel, supplies, and equipment via all modes of transportation. In the
performance of their duties, they support the administrative requirements,
applicable maintenance, command and control of transportation throughput via
beaches, landing zones, ports, and terminals used in support of MAGTF
operations and deployments. Additionally, they are trained to facilitate
operations at naval ports, arrival/departure airfield, helicopter support,
and rail head operations. At the SNCO level, Logistics Specialist serve
within these functional areas at the J/G/S-4 as section level supervisors.
Additional billets outside the Fleet Marine Force includes serving as combat
cargo assistants (CCAs) onboard naval amphibious warfare ships.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must possess a GT score of 100 or higher.

            (3) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.




                                            3-47                        Enclosure (1)
 3111                                                                   NAVMC 1200.1L



        (4) Logistics/Mobility follow-on courses that enhance MOS proficiency
are identified in the current version of the MOS Roadmap within the Marine
Corps Training Information Management System (MCTIMS). Listed courses
outline which course directly contribute to the growth of the 0441.

        (5) The completion of listed courses enhances proficiency and
increases the probability of Marines being promoted to the next grade.
Marines who complete all identified courses will be viewed has highly
competitive for promotion and set themselves apart from their peers.

        (6) These courses and their completion coincide with requirements
identified within the most current version on the Logistics Training and
Readiness Manual which contribute to the professional capability of the
individual Marine and capacity within the logistics community.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Basic Logistics Course (M030DQ7), Logistics
Operations School, Marine Corps Combat Service Support Schools, Camp Johnson/
Camp Lejeune, NC.

        (2) Marines making a lateral move must also complete the Basic
Logistics Course (M030DQ7), Logistics Operations School, Marine Corps Combat
Service Support Schools, Camp Johnson/Camp Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (f), Logistics Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Cargo and Freight Agent 43-5011.

            (2) Production, Planning and Expediting Clerks 43-5061.

        (3) Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialist
and Crew Members, all other 55-3019.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Distribution Specialist, 3152.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
